question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
I could not find anything in the indexed bills that answers this question.

Closest bills by title: National Building Research Institute (551/2024, 621/2025, 629/2025); Nation Building Tax (Amendment) (003/2014, 016/2013, 017/2020, 030/2020, 043/2019, 056/2019, 112/2016, 210/2017); Shop and Office Employees (Regulation of Employment and Remuneration) (Amendment) (039/2020, 044/2020, 414/2023, 442/2024, 545/2024, 553/2024).

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
Deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act are excluded from subsection (2) **for any year of assessment prior to April 1, 2018**.  

- §37(2A)(a) of the Inland Revenue (Amendment) – GS, 2026‑02‑24【013/2026 §37】.  

Caveats: The amendment only applies to prior‑2018 years; it does not affect deductions claimed from April 1, 2018 onward.

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
A licence issued or renewed under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law is valid for **one year**.  

- Validity period: one year [645/2025 §25]  
- Licence may be renewed by application before expiry [645/2025 §24].

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer: A container depot operator must submit a renewal application **at least thirty days before the licence expires**【657/2025 §6】.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
The amendment allows a freezing order to remain in force for **up to two years**.  
- “not exceeding two years” replaces the former limit of one year【020/2026 §8】.  
- The order itself is now valid for “a period of fourteen working days” before further action【020/2026 §8】.  
- No other duration limits appear in the evidence.

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer:
The levy is calculated on the value of the telecom services received **each month** [028/2026 §2].  

- The charge is imposed “on the receipt of such telecommunication services in respect of each month” [028/2026 §2].  

Caveats: The rate applied depends on the schedule and the period of service.

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer: The amended Ordinance allows a notice of a bill’s refusal or non‑payment to be given **in writing, by personal communication, by facsimile transmission, or by any other electronic means that sufficiently identify the bill**.[601/2025 §8]

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
A qualified auditor is anyone who is either

* an individual who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka, or any other Institute established by law, and holds a certificate to practice as an accountant issued by that Institute’s Council; or  
* a firm of accountants whose resident partners each are members of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka or any other Institute established by law and hold such a certificate.

[626/2025 §11]

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer: “Knowledge sharing activities” are those activities “designed to facilitate the exchange of ideas, skills and experiences fostering a culture of learning and collaboration.” [646/2025 §18]

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The Society may acquire, hold and manage any movable or immovable property that becomes vested in it by purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise, and it may sell, mortgage, lease, exchange or otherwise dispose of that property, subject to rules made under section 7.  

- Ability to take and hold any property vested in it – purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition, etc. [047/2026 §13]  
- Power to sell, mortgage, lease, exchange or otherwise dispose of the property. [047/2026 §13]  
- All such actions are subject to rules made under section 7 of the Act. [047/2026 §7]

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
I could not find anything in the indexed bills that answers this question.

Closest bills by title: Institute of Real Estate Professionals, Sri Lanka (637/2025, 656/2025); Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka (040/2026, 050/2026); Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka (Incorporation) (172/2022, 175/2022, 597/2025, 608/2025).

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Workers hired by businesses that already held a Colombo Port City licence before the amendment can be paid in foreign currency and their employment income is exempt from Sri Lankan income tax for three years. Employees hired by businesses that receive a licence after the amendment are subject to normal income‑tax treatment.  

- Licences issued before the amendment: 3‑year income‑tax exemption for resident and non‑resident staff paid in foreign currency. [652/2025 §3]  
- Licences issued on or after the amendment’s commencement: employment income liable to income tax. [652/2025 §3]  
- The exemption applies to both resident and non‑resident employees. [652/2025 §3]

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The amendment removes the phrase “and Container Operators” from the Act’s long title, changing it to  

**“Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders and Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers Act.”**  

- Substitution of the long‑title words shown in §3(1)(a) [658/2025 §3].  
- The same substitution is noted in §2 for the title wording [658/2025 §2].  
- The change deletes all references to “container operators” from the title.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act (Section 16A) removes the old definition of “finance business” and replaces the definition of “funds or property” with a new, wider definition of “funds, property or other assets” that covers currency, property, virtual assets, legal documents, etc. It also inserts new definitions for “armed conflict”, “computer data”, “computer system” and “foreign terrorist fighter”.  

- Repeal of “finance business” definition – [018/2026 §16]  
- New definition of “funds, property or other assets” – [018/2026 §16]  
- New definitions (“armed conflict”, “computer data”, etc.) – [018/2026 §16]

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
The 2025 bill that sets out the budget and borrowing limits for the 2026 financial year is the **Appropriation Act, No. 2025 (Bill 639/2025)**.  
- It authorises expenditure of Rs 4 434.356 billion for 2026 and borrowing up to Rs 3 800 billion, with loan details to be reported in the Final Budget Position Report.  
- It allows advances from the Consolidated Fund, Treasury reallocations, and requires parliamentary approval for changes.  
- The same provisions appear in Bill 632/2025, an “Appropriation (Other)” version of the Act.  

[639/2025 §2]

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. 2026** (Bill 043/2026, gazetted 2026‑06‑15; Bill 055/2026, presented 2026‑07‑27) creates the foundation.

- Establishes a corporate body to promote economic and social development in Sri Lanka.  
- Grants powers to sue, be sued, own property, borrow money, receive donations (foreign funds require Dept. of External Resources approval).  
- Sets non‑discriminatory objectives: rural training, micro‑entrepreneurship, drug‑abuse prevention, soil conservation, etc.  

**Caveats:** No penalties are specified, and the two versions are identical in substance.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
The Council may suspend a member for **no longer than one year** in lieu of disenrolment.  
- “warn, reprimand or suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year”【054/2026 §24】.

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, a person must have been in **undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation for more than three months** to be regarded as an “occupant.”  

- [004/2026 §2] “has been in undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation of such premises for a period of more than three months…”  
- [634/2025 §2] (GS) repeats the same wording.  

No other time‑limit is specified in the bill.

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
I could not find anything in the indexed bills that answers this question.

Closest bills by title: Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority (398/2023, 450/2024, 645/2025, 653/2025); Gambling Regulatory Authority (594/2025, 613/2025); Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) (036/2020, 044/2026, 047/2020, 056/2026).

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
The amendment allows imprisonment of up to **one year** for a person who arrives in or departs Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit.  

- Imprisonment “for a term not exceeding one year” – [021/2026 §31]

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
The member must pay a **late payment fee equal to twice the annual subscription** if the subscription is not paid by the 31 December deadline.  
- Late fee: twice the annual subscription, payable by 30 April of the following year. [072/2026 §30]

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The body corporate must pay all debts and liabilities that existed **the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of the Act**.  

- “All debts and liabilities of the Trust existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act…” [009/2026 §12] (also identical in 095/2021 §12).

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer:
A master or captain who fails to report such a passenger or crew member faces a fine only: **₹100 000 minimum and ₹500 000 maximum**.

- Fine range: ₹100 000–₹500 000 on conviction.  
  [082/2026 §90]

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer:
The Board Chairman serves for **three years** and may be re‑appointed.  
- “The Chairman so appointed shall hold office for a term of three years and shall be eligible for reappointment.”【636/2025 §11】

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The amended Act replaces every reference to “Controller” or “Rubber Controller” with the “Director‑General of the Rubber Development Department.”  

- Substitution clause: “Controller” and “Rubber Controller” → “Director‑General” [595/2025 §2].  
- Reference to the Director‑General: “Director‑General of the Rubber Development Department” [595/2025 §2].

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, a “public authority” is understood to be a ministry, a government department or a public corporation (the judiciary is excluded from this list).  

- Ministries, government departments and public corporations are treated as public authorities.  
- The judiciary acting in its judicial capacity is not considered a public authority for purposes of the Act.  

[152/2021 §20]

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka (Incorporation) law, a “qualified auditor” is defined as:

- an individual who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka or any other institute established by law **and** possesses a certificate to practice as an accountant issued by the Council of that institute;  
- or a firm of accountants whose resident partners each are members of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka or another legally established institute **and** possess such a certificate.  

[597/2025 §10]

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
An investigation officer may use the following advanced techniques only after a magistrate’s authorization:

- Controlled delivery of suspected assets or information.  
- Digital surveillance, including interception and recording of digital, voice and video communications.  
- Undercover operations, including the use of decoys.  
- Laying of traps.  
- Forensic extraction of data, information and images from computers, mobile phones, digital storage devices and other digital equipment.  

[570/2025 §60] lists each of these methods as subject to magistrate approval.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
Five council members must be present, and the Chairperson must be one of those five to form a quorum.  
- Quorum: five members including the Chairperson [054/2026 §7].  
- The Chairperson must be among the five present [054/2026 §7].

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
The National Transport Commission must compute bus‑and‑other‑service fares by applying a formula it sets from time to time, publish the resulting fare list on its official website, and transport operators must prepare a fare list that follows that published list and display it conspicuously on each vehicle. The Commission may inspect compliance, and failure to comply is an offence under section 40.  

- Commission computes fares using a formula it determines from time to time, following the national policy approved by Parliament and an Order published in the Gazette. [577/2025 §19]  
- Commission publishes the fare lists on its official website; operators must prepare a list in accordance with those published lists. [577/2025 §19]  
- Operators must display the fare list at any conspicuous place on the vehicle, and the Commission may inspect compliance. [577/2025 §19]  

Caveats: The specific formula and order are not detailed in the provided text.

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
The Mass Foundation will be a corporate body with **perpetual succession** under the name “Mass Foundation” and may **sue and be sued** with full power and authority. Its **seal** may only be affixed when two Committee members sign, and it is kept in the custody of a Committee office‑bearer. The Foundation is classified as a **voluntary social service organization** for regulatory purposes under the Voluntary Social Service Organizations (Registration and Supervision) Act, No 31 of 1980.  

- Perpetual succession & legal personality: [025/2026 §2]  
- Litigatory power: [025/2026 §2]  
- Seal usage & custody: [025/2026 §15]  
- Regulatory classification: [025/2026 §2]

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
The amendment treats **the Minister assigned to the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (or the Minister assigned to the subject of industries) under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution** as the “Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government” for Part III when a water‑supply or sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board.  
- In the amendment, the phrase “the Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government” is read as “the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka established under the Board of Investment Law, No. 4 of 1978 under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution or the Minister assigned the subject of industries under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution” [019/2026 §10].  
- The evidence does not include the part of the amendment that explicitly states that this substitution applies to Part III of the Act; that passage is missing.  
- No other ministerial substitution is provided for this scenario.

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
The magistrate must actively supervise the approved detention centre.  
- Visit the centre once a month, interview the suspects and examine their well‑being, and inspect detention registers, orders and other required books【078/2026 §33】.  
- The authority in charge must give the magistrate prompt, unimpeded access【078/2026 §33】.  
- If the magistrate first heard the suspect, he may also visit and exercise the same powers【078/2026 §33】.  

Caveats: The provisions apply only to centres that have been formally approved under the bill.

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
The Bill applies to **any civil or commercial dispute** that is not already governed by the Mediation Boards Act No. 72 of 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act No. 21 of 2003.  

- Applies to all civil and commercial disputes by mediation, whether by agreement or court‑referral.  
- Excludes disputes that fall under the Mediation Boards Act 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act 2003.  
- Disputes required to be mediated under those two acts cannot be mediated under this Bill.  

[622/2025 §2]

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
The amendment requires that the accounts of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies be audited under the same rules that apply to public corporations, namely the provisions of Article 154 of the Constitution and the National Audit Act No 19 of 2018.  

- Article 154 of the Constitution and National Audit Act No 19 of 2018 apply to the audit of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies【600/2025 §3】.  
- The same provisions also apply to Samurdhi community‑based banks (section 28A)【600/2025 §2】.  
- No new penalties are introduced by the amendment.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
A struck‑off company may apply to a court within ten years, showing cause to the Attorney‑General, and the court may re‑register it and order the return of all property that had previously vested in the State under section 487.  

- Re‑registration and return of property – [582/2025 §17] (identical in [541/2024 §15]).  
- If the State has dealt with or disposed of the property, third‑party rights acquired in good faith are unaffected.  
- If the property has been destroyed, damaged, or not taken, the State is not liable.  

**Caveats**: The evidence does not detail what happens if re‑registration is denied, or how assets already disposed of are handled beyond the stated protections.

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
A person charged with a corruption offence will be denied bail if the offence involves a bribe of at least Rs 100 000, or the corruption has caused the Government a loss of at least Rs 500 000, or has enabled the accused (or another person) to obtain a benefit, favour or advantage of at least Rs 500 000 that the Director‑General certifies. In those cases bail is “non‑bailable except in exceptional circumstances by a High Court.”  

- Bribe ≥ Rs 100 000 – [063/2026 §17]  
- Loss to Govt ≥ Rs 500 000 – [063/2026 §17]  
- Benefit/favour/advantage ≥ Rs 500 000 confirmed by DG – [063/2026 §17]  

Caveats: The provisions apply only to offences under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act and do not cover other offences.

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
Offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule are treated as **non‑political** for extradition purposes; Sri Lanka may extradite a suspect to any UN member state without regard to a political‑offence classification.  

- They are “deemed not to be an offence of a political character … for the purposes only of extradition … between the Government of Sri Lanka and any UN Member State.” [073/2026 §11]  
- This treatment overrides any contrary provisions in the Extradition Law, No. 8 of 1977. [073/2026 §11]  
- The same rule applies when Sri Lanka affords assistance to a UN member state under section 12. [073/2026 §11]

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the revised National Environmental Act, a person convicted of an offence under Section 23r faces a fine of **between ₹100 000 and ₹1 000 000**. If the offence continues after conviction, an **additional ₹5 000 per day** is imposed for each day the offence persists.

- Fine range: ₹100 000–₹1 000 000 before the Magistrate having jurisdiction [032/2026 §18].
- Daily continuation penalty: ₹5 000 per day if the offence continues after conviction [032/2026 §18].

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?
answer:
The amendment raises the penalty for the offence in Section 42 to **a fine not exceeding 100 000 rupees, or imprisonment not exceeding one year, or both**.  

- Fine up to 100 000 rupees [611/2025 §13]  
- Imprisonment up to 1 year [611/2025 §13]  
- Or both (fine and imprisonment) [611/2025 §13]

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?
answer:
The owner must pay a fine of **two thousand rupees** plus the ordinary registration fee, and the local authority is required to **immediately vaccinate and register the dog**.  

- Fine: Rs 2 000, plus the registration fee – [066/2026 §7] (4).  
- Additional action: the local authority shall vaccinate and register the dog immediately – [066/2026 §7] (4).

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
The amendment adds **methamphetamine** to the list of named narcotics, replacing the earlier list of “heroin or cocaine or morphine or opium” with “heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine”【068/2026 §2】. It also creates a new offence for manufacturing any dangerous drug in Groups A‑E (other than those five drugs) and imposes a fine of ₹200,000‑₹500,000, imprisonment of 10‑20 years, or both【068/2026 §2】.  

- New drug added: methamphetamine【068/2026 §2】.  
- New penalty: fine ₹200,000‑₹500,000, 10‑20 years imprisonment, or both【068/2026 §2】.  
- Offence applies to manufacturing any Group A‑E drug except the five named narcotics【068/2026 §2】.

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?
answer:
No – the repeal ends all benefits that the 1986 Act gave to former presidents and their widows, so none of those entitlements will continue once the new Act takes effect.  

- The Act declares the 1986 Presidents’ Entitlements Act repealed, so any residence, monthly allowance, secretarial allowance, official transport or widow’s pension provided under it ceases. [624/2025 §3]  
- No new powers, duties or penalties are created; the only effect is the removal of the former entitlements. [627/2025]  
- The cessation occurs from the commencement date of the repeal Act, after which those payments and facilities are no longer provided. [624/2025 §3]

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?
answer:
The amendment adds a new section (316a) that punishes a person who “voluntarily causes grievous hurt to a person under eighteen years of age” with imprisonment for up to **ten years** and, in addition, a fine and compensation for the victim.  

- Imprisonment up to 10 years – [618/2025 §6]  
- Fine and compensation – [618/2025 §6]

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The 023/2026 amendment removes the earlier 120‑million‑rupee ceiling, shortens the 60‑million‑rupee ceiling to the period before 1 April 2026, and adds a new 36‑million‑rupee limit for four‑quarter turnover after that date.

- Paragraph (b) no longer contains the “hundred and twenty million rupees; or” threshold [017/2026 §3 (1)].
- Paragraph (c) now reads “on or after January 1 2024 and prior to April 1 2026” and keeps the 60‑million‑rupee ceiling [017/2026 §3 (2)].
- New paragraph (d) states that for any period commencing on or after April 1 2026 the aggregate turnover for four consecutive quarters “does not exceed thirty‑six million rupees” [017/2026 §3 (3)].

**Caveat:** The amendment only modifies Section 5; further provisions on registration and other aspects are not covered here.

question: What changes does the amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act make to the ownership percentage requirement and to the type of entities mentioned in its subsections?
answer:
The amendment changes Section 14 so that the ownership threshold is now **100 %** (instead of “more than 50 %”) and the parties referred to in subsections (2) and (3) must be **companies incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007** rather than generic persons.  

- Subsection (1): “more than fifty per centum” → “one hundred per centum”【584/2025 §12】.  
- Subsection (2): “Any person who” → “Any company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, which”【584/2025 §12】.  
- Subsection (3): “a person who” → “a company, which”【584/2025 §12】.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Trusts Ordinance, which part of Section 3 is being removed and how is the definition of “express trust” being changed?
answer:
The amendment repeals **paragraph (n)** of Section 3.  
In paragraph (p) the definition of “express trust” is altered by **substituting “trust in the form” for the words “trust generally in the form.”**  

- Repeal: paragraph (n) of Section 3 – [081/2026 §2]  
- Definition change: replace “trust generally in the form” with “trust in the form” – [081/2026 §2]

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
Judges are permitted to serve until **63 years** (up from 61), while **all other judges and magistrates must retire at 62 years**.

- Judges: “sixty‑three years” replaces “sixty‑one years” in subsection (3) of Section 6. [058/2026 §3]  
- Other judges & magistrates: new subsection (4) sets retirement age at “sixty‑two years”. [058/2026 §3]

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Universities Act, how many terms is a person allowed to serve as dean of a faculty?
answer:
A person may serve as dean for **no more than two terms** under the proposed amendment.  

- New subsection (4) of §2 of the amendment: “No person shall be appointed as the Dean of a Faculty for more than two terms.” [649/2025 §2]

question: What 2025 legislation establishes the professional facilities‑management institute as a legal corporate body in Sri Lanka?
answer: Bill 623/2025 – the Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (Incorporation) Act creates the Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (IFMSL) as a legal corporate body. [623/2025]

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
The legal corporation is created by the **Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. of 2025** – Bill 596/2025 (also gazetted as GS 581/2025).  

- Bill 596/2025 incorporates the foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the power to sue and be sued. [596/2025 §1]  
- The same text appears in the gazetted version GS 581/2025, confirming the act’s enactment. [581/2025]

question: What 2026 amendment revises the Act that governs marriage and divorce among the Kandyan community (Chapter 113)?
answer:
The 2026 amendment is the **Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment) Act, No. of 2026** (GS 008/2026 and Bill 016/2026).  

- It amends Section 32 of the Kandyan Marriage and Divorce Act (Chapter 113) by replacing paragraph (a) with “Adultery by the husband or wife after marriage” and repealing paragraph (b) [008/2026 §2].

question: What is the 2026 legislation that establishes the Al‑Hashimi Association as a legal corporate entity?
answer:
The Al‑Hashimi Association is incorporated under the **Al‑Hashimi Association (Incorporation) Act, Bill 024/2026** (Gazetted 2026‑04‑08).  

- Bill 024/2026 creates the body corporate and declares its objects and powers. [024/2026 §3]  
- The preamble states the association is to be incorporated for public advantage. [024/2026]  
- The Act is published in the Gazette before presentation. [024/2026]

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2026 bill that repeals the 2009 Chief of Defence Staff Act is **Bill 059/2026 – “Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Act”**.  

- §2 of the bill states the repeal: “The Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 is hereby repealed” [059/2026 §2].  
- The bill’s provisions set out the consequences of the repeal, such as the cessation of the office and transfer of property to the Ministry of Defence [059/2026 §3].  
- A Gazette‑issued version (GS 036/2026) contains the identical text.  

Caveats: The bill is presented as Bill 059/2026; the earlier Gazette version (036/2026) is the published form.

question: What 2025 legislation modifies the 1988 Provincial Councils Elections Act in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 legislation is the **Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment) Act, No. 2025** (Bill 605/2025 and GS 589/2025).  

- Restores the 1988 Act as it stood on 21 September 2017, overriding Act No 17 of 2017 [589/2025 §2].  
- Applies to all provincial council elections and takes effect from the date it comes into force [589/2025 §1].  
- Sinhala text prevails if Sinhala and Tamil versions differ [589/2025 §1].  

*Caveats*: the exact coming‑into‑force date is not specified in the evidence.

question: Which 2025 bill amends the 2016 Act that provides a financial assistance scheme for workers?
answer:
The 2025 amendment to the 2016 financial‑assistance scheme is **Bill 602/2025 – Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) Act**.  
- It amends Section 3 of the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 4 of 2016 to extend the allowance period until 31 March 2025. [602/2025 §2]  
- The Gazetteed version of the same amendment is Bill 587/2025. [587/2025]

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 bill that amends the 2016 minimum‑wage law is the **National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment) Bill 604/2025** (the Gazetteed version is GS 586/2025). It amends Section 3 of the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016.  

- Bill 604/2025 amends Section 3 of the 2016 Act, repealing subsection (1) and substituting new wage levels【604/2025 §2】.  
- The Gazetteed version (GS 586/2025) contains identical text and also states it amends the 2016 Act【586/2025】.  

**Caveat** – The bill is presented as Bill 604/2025; its earlier Gazetteed form is GS 586/2025.

question: Which 2025 amendment alters the 2005 law that established the workers' special financial assistance allowance?
answer:
The 2025 amendment is the **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) – Bill 603/2025** (presented 2025‑06‑03).  
- It amends Section 3(1) of the 2005 Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, replacing “with effect from August 1 2005” with “for the period commencing on August 1 2005 and ending on March 31 2025”【603/2025】.  
- The amendment contains no new powers, duties or penalties; it merely revises the time‑frame wording【588/2025 §2】.

question: What 2026 legislation proposes to abolish the 1977 law that provided retirement benefits to Sri Lankan parliamentarians?
answer:
The bill is **Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal) Bill 001/2026** (presented 7 January 2026) which repeals the Parliamentary Pensions Law, No. 1 of 1977.  

- Repeals the 1977 law providing retirement benefits to parliamentarians. [001/2026 §2]

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The 2025 bill was **Bill 642/2025 – Betting and Gaming Levy (Amendment)**, which amends the Betting and Gaming Levy Act No 40 of 1988 (the tax on gambling).  

- Bill 642/2025 changes the levy rates for betting and gaming operators and revises Section 2 of the 1988 Act. [642/2025]

question: Which 2025 bill proposes changes to the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)?
answer:
The 2025 bill that amends the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464) is **Bill 625/2025 – Land Development (Amendment) Bill**【625/2025】.  

- Removes the phrase “or upon his or her marriage” from §48A 2(c).  
- Deletes subsection 48B 1(a).  
- Rewrites §68(1) to require “fails without reasonable cause” to be deemed non‑compliant.

question: Which 2026 bill updates the 2018 Finance Act No. 35?
answer:
The 2026 bill that amends the 2018 Finance Act No. 35 is the **Finance (Amendment) Act, 2026 – Bill 034/2026**.  
- It amends Section 44 of the Finance Act No. 35 of 2018 to give a five‑year levy exemption for newly constructed cellular towers commencing operation on or after 1 January 2026. [034/2026 §2]  
- The same amendment appears in the Gazette‑published version 027/2026, but the Bill presented to Parliament is 034/2026. [027/2026]  
- The Act may be cited as the Finance (Amendment) Act, No. of 2026. [034/2026 §1]

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
The 2026 bill that revises the 1956 Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act is **Bill 056/2026 – Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) Act, No. 2026**.  

- Raises fines in sections 7, 13 and 20a from ten thousand rupees to one hundred thousand rupees.  
- Amendments apply only to offences committed after the Act comes into force.  
- Sinhala text prevails where Sinhala and Tamil texts differ.  

[056/2026 §1]

question: Which 2025 bill proposes to revoke the 2024 legislation that introduced internet safety and content regulation measures?
answer:
The 2025 bill that seeks to revoke the 2024 online‑safety law is **Bill 590/2025 – Online Safety (Repeal) – Bill**.  

- It cites itself as “Online Safety (Repeal) Act, No. of 2025” and declares that the Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024 is hereby repealed. [590/2025 §1]  
- It expressly repeals any regulations made under the 2024 Act from the date of enactment of this Act. [590/2025 §3]  
- A Gazette‑issued version (GS 578/2025) contains identical provisions. [578/2025 §2]  

*No other 2025 bill in the evidence proposes such a repeal.*

question: What 2025 legislation addresses re‑conducting postponed local council elections by allowing new nominations and setting a fresh election date?
answer:
The 2025 law is the **Local Authorities Elections (Special Provisions) Act 2025** (Bill 566/2025, gazetted as 565/2025). It nullifies the 2023 nominations, orders fresh nomination papers and sets a new election date within three months of the Act’s coming into force.  

- Fresh nominations are required; earlier papers are deemed void [566/2025] p.2.  
- The Election Commission must publish new nomination notices within three months [565/2025 §3].  
- Deposits paid under the Ordinance are refunded on proof of receipt [565/2025 §2].  

Caveats: the bill and gazette version are identical; no further amendment details are provided.

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 bill that updates the 2008 act governing major strategic development projects is **Bill 650/2025 – Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) – Bill (2025‑11‑14)**.  

- Amends the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008. [650/2025]

question: Which 2026 bill was introduced to legally establish the UnV charitable foundation?
answer:
The UnV Foundation was legally established by Bill 010/2026 – “UnV Foundation (Incorporation) – Bill” presented on 22 January 2026.  

- Bill 010/2026 incorporates the UnV Foundation as a body corporate.  
- The same text appears unchanged in the Gazette version 003/2026 (GS, 2026‑01‑09).  

[010/2026 §1] [010/2026 §12]

question: Which 2025 bill updates Sri Lanka's 1979 criminal procedure legislation?
answer:
Bill 576/2025 – the **Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Bill** updates the 1979 Code of Criminal Procedure Act No 15.

- Inserts sections 144A and 144B, allowing a magistrate to dispense with a suspect’s or accused’s personal court attendance under special circumstances【576/2025 §2】.  
- Same amendment text also appears in Bill 579/2025, but the primary amendment is Bill 576/2025.

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
The 2026 bill is **Bill 065/2026 – “Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution.”**  
- Bill number and title: Bill 065/2026 – Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution [065/2026 §2].  
- The Gazette version of the same amendment was published as GS 057/2026 (same text) [057/2026 §1].

question: Which 2026 bill seeks to repeal the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2026 bill that repeals the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) is **Bill 006/2026 – Rent (Repeal) Bill**.

- It expressly repeals the Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972. [006/2026]  
- The bill is titled “Rent (Repeal) – Bill” and was presented on 20 January 2026. [006/2026]

question: What 2026 legislation creates a corporate entity for the Mahawilachchiya children’s education centre?
answer:
The 2026 legislation that creates the corporate entity is **Bill 011/2026 – Mahawilachchiya Education Centre for Children (Incorporation)**, published in the Gazette 2026‑02‑06.  

- It establishes a body corporate called the Mahawilachchiya Centre for Education for Children, a perpetual non‑profit.  
- The centre is classified as a Voluntary Social Services Organization, so the 1980 Voluntary Social Services Organisations Act applies.  
- The body may own or lease property, sign contracts, borrow money, receive donations (foreign funds require Department of External Resources approval), open bank accounts, invest surplus, employ staff, and run IT‑training programmes for rural youth.  

[011/2026 §3]
